findings.summary: The C# ByteLimitField/ByteLimitUnits mapping has no production caller; the page JS is a mirrored copy that no test executes.
findings.detail: ADRs require the unit/step/precision mapping to be code-owned per field, but the settings page is a static embedded resource (src/ArrTags/Configuration/config.html) that cannot invoke C#. The C# helper is therefore the code-owned contract consumed by the test suite, and the page duplicates unit/unitBytes/stepBytes/precision in its byteLimitFields table. ByteLimitSettingsPageTests pins the table rows and the native min/max/step/label attributes structurally against the C# mapping, and pins the presence of the conversion/step-check snippets, but does not execute the JS algorithm. The repository has no JS runtime/test infrastructure (no in-tree JS runner; node/nodejs/deno/bun/qjs/js/d8/jsc are absent from this environment), so this is inherent to the established page architecture, not a shortcut introduced by this task. The worker disclosed it in known_limitations.
evidence: src/ArrTags/Configuration/ByteLimitField.cs (no production callers; grep confirms only tests/ByteLimitUnitsTests.cs and the page mirror reference the mapping)
No node/nodejs/deno/bun/qjs/js/d8/jsc on PATH; no in-tree package.json test runner
findings.recommended_action: No change required for 16.1; the 16.6 integration verification may record that the page algorithm is confirmed only structurally (or on a live host), as already noted.

findings.summary: Legacy in-range off-step persisted values change on save: whole-unit fields are adjusted to the nearest whole unit; 64-KiB-step fields reject the save until edited.
findings.detail: ADR-028 clause 1 promises exact round-trip only at each field's minimum, default, and maximum; it does not promise round-trip for arbitrary persisted bytes. The pre-16.1 page accepted any in-range integer, so an upgraded ArrTags.xml can hold an off-step value. Such a value loads, validates, activates, and serializes unchanged, which satisfies the acceptance criterion 'an existing ArrTags.xml loads unchanged' (proved by ByteLimitUnitsTests.AnExistingConfigurationWithAnOffStepByteValueStillLoadsUnchanged, which exercises PluginConfigurationValidator.Validate, ConfigurationSnapshotService activation, and the XmlSerializer boundary). On save, the page renders the stored bytes at the fixed precision and converts back with the step check: for the whole-KiB/whole-MiB fields the display is an integer unit so the write is a valid step multiple (silently adjusted by at most half a display unit), and for the three 64-KiB-step MB fields the save is rejected unless the rounded display value is itself a step multiple. This is the ADR-028 reject-rather-than-round behaviour applied at the display precision, and it is disclosed in both the task 16.1 changelog entry and the worker report's known_limitations. The persisted XML is never rewritten without a save, and the numeric range semantics are unchanged.
evidence: docs/decisions/ADR-028.md clause 1 (exact round-trip only at min/default/max; off-step rejected)
src/ArrTags/Configuration/config.html byteLimitToBytes step check; git diff shows no change to OperationalLimits.cs / PluginConfigurationValidator.cs
findings.recommended_action: Accepted as an ADR-028 consequence; task 16.6 should consider registering it in docs/limitations/ as already planned. No change required for 16.1.

findings.summary: The worker's probe-B failure count (9) is slightly higher than a static recount of affected cases suggests (~7); immaterial to the sensitivity conclusion.
findings.detail: Removing the trailing-zero trim in FormatScaled affects only precision>0 fields. A static count of the test cases whose expected strings contain trimmed zeros yields roughly four DisplayUsesTheFixedUnitAndPrecisionWithTrailingZerosTrimmed cases (Provider '1'/'8'/'64', Source '128') plus three RangeLabelStaysInTheFieldUnitAndShowsTheSubMebibyteBoundAsAFraction cases (Provider/Source/Derived) = ~7, versus the report's stated 6 + 3 = 9. Other probes' counts are consistent (e.g. probe A: 7 off-step cases + the ADR example = 8). The discrepancy is a recording imprecision in the sensitivity narrative; it does not affect the conclusion that the tests are sensitive to the trim, and no acceptance criterion depends on the exact count. The probes themselves could not be re-run because the reviewer is read-only for product code.
findings.recommended_action: No action; note for future reports to keep probe failure counts exact. Does not affect approval.
